LESSON: POSITION AND DIRECTION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.1: Position and Direction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Position and Direction, part of Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you changeyour position?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Make clockwise or anticlockwise turns in the environment. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or teachers to perform the task.

2. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups and demonstrate a clockwise turn. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Make clockwise or anticlockwise turns in the environment. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or teachers to perform the task.
2. Discuss in purposive pairs or groups and demonstrate a clockwise turn. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Position and Direction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner works collaboratively with others while making clockwise or anticlockwise turns in

the environment.

Values:
Unity: learner embraces others as they demonstrate a clockwise turn.

51

Learner observes care and precautions while making quarter, half and full turns in the environment to enhance

safety.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate making quarter, half and full turns in the surroundings to the Location, Position and

size of Kenya in Social Studies.
